subject: Subprocessor key escrow and HSM attestation for MedWorks integration
messages:
From: Alice Turner <alice.turner@medworks.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@medworks.com
Date: 2027-02-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Subprocessor key escrow / HSM attestation request

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the call this morning. As part of our vendor onboarding checklist we need written confirmation of how Redwood and any listed subprocessors handle key escrow and authority over encryption keys used to protect customer data. Specifically MedWorks requires: 

- Whether keys are retained by Redwood or by subprocessors; if retained by subprocessors, which subprocessors and locations.
- Evidence that keys are generated and stored in FIPS 140-2/3 HSMs, including attestation or SOC/AICPA-style statements where available.
- The certificate chain used for signing attestation, or an HSM vendor statement (e.g., AWS CloudHSM, Azure Key Vault HSM).
- A diagram showing dataflow for customer model encryption keys and any escrow/recovery flows.

Can you send a short attestation and evidence bundle (PDF + diagrams) and a filled SIG/CAIQ matrix rows relevant to crypto key management? Our procurement team needs these by EOD Monday to hit our compliance window.

Appreciate it — happy to loop in your compliance contact if easier.

Best,
Alice
Alice Turner
Manager, Security & Assurance | MedWorks


From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Turner <alice.turner@medworks.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-20T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor key escrow / HSM attestation request

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary up front: Redwood does not escrow customer encryption keys to any third party by default. Customer model keys may be backed up via our optional Recovery Key Escrow service (customer opt-in) which stores an encrypted escrow blob in a customer-controlled KMS with HSM-backed envelopes. When escrow is enabled the envelope keys are managed in FIPS 140-2/3 HSMs (AWS CloudHSM or Azure Dedicated HSM) depending on region and customer choice.

I’m attaching a short attestation and a diagram and will pass your HSM request to our security team for the signed evidence. For the SIG/CAIQ rows we've filled the crypto key management and key lifecycle sections and attached the workbook (sig_response_matrix.xlsx).

Attachments: redwood_hsm_attestation.pdf (attestation summary), subprocessor_kv_keyflow-diagram.png (dataflow), sig_response_matrix.xlsx

Next steps I recommend: 
- We’ll provide the signed HSM vendor statement (or notarized attestation) by EOD Monday.
- Monica will supply the certificate chain and any vendor reference numbers.
- If MedWorks requires keys be held only within a specific HSM vendor, we can confirm compatibility and routing rules in the Dedicated configuration.

Looping in Monica and Karthik to take point on evidence. Marissa — tell procurement the delivery ETA is EOD Monday and flag if a DocuSign attestation is needed.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
log an.wright@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 415-555-0192

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Turner <alice.turner@medworks.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-20T15:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor key escrow / HSM attestation request

Hi Alice,

Following up with technical evidence. Short answers: 
- Escrow: optional customer-controlled escrow only; default is no escrow.
- HSMs: We use AWS CloudHSM (us-west-2) and Azure Dedicated HSM (uksouth / eastus) for envelope key management depending on customer region. Both are FIPS 140-2/3 validated.
- Subprocessors: The only subprocessor that may hold or operate HSM-backed envelopes on our behalf for some customers is our managed-disk encryption partner (CipherLane Inc.). Where CipherLane is used, all envelopes remain wrapped by customer KMS keys; CipherLane does not possess plaintext keys. CipherLane contractually prohibits exporting customer plaintext keys.

Requested evidence attached: 
- redwood_hsm_attestation.pdf (signed attestation describing flows and HSM vendors)
- cipherlane_subproc_statement.pdf (signed by CipherLane; limited distribution — available on NDA)
- subprocessor_kv_keyflow-diagram.png (labeled flows)
- sig_response_matrix.xlsx (relevant CAIQ/SIG rows filled)

Certificate chain: The attestation is signed with Redwood’s P-256 signing cert (CN=redwood-compliance-2026), and the vendor HSM statements include vendor-signed metadata. If MedWorks needs the full chain and CA fingerprints, let me know and I’ll export them (or share via secure drive).

If you need a DocuSign-signed letter on letterhead, we can produce one but will need a PO/DocuSign routing contact.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai

From: Alice Turner <alice.turner@medworks.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@medworks.com
Date: 2027-02-21T16:38:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor key escrow / HSM attestation request

Monica — this is great, thanks. A couple of quick clarifications before we close the vendor assessment: 

1) Can you confirm whether CipherLane processes any escrow envelope unwrap operations outside the primary region (we need assurance that unwrapping is constrained to region-bound HSMs)?
2) Can we get the certificate fingerprints (SHA256) for the attestation signing cert and the HSM vendor statement?
3) If we request DocuSign-signed attestation on letterhead, our procurement will provide the DocuSign recipient and PO. Please advise if Redwood requires any additional paperwork for that flow.

If you can answer 1+2 in-line and provide the fingerprint list, procurement will mark the security review as complete. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Alice
